notes: Every documented v1 route is served under https://api.raindrop.io/rest/v1, so the prefix is part of each reviewed path rather than of the origin.
An access token, including a test token, is documented as carried in Authorization: Bearer with no second token header.
GET /rest/v1/user returns a result flag plus a user object whose _id is an integer and whose fullName is a string of at most 1000 characters. Nullability is not documented for either.

GET /rest/v1/collections returns a result flag plus items, and each item is a collection object whose identifier is _id, with documented title, count and view fields. There is no hidden field on a collection; hidden exists only on a group inside the user document.
The documentation warns that responses can contain fields it does not describe and that using them is unsafe, so only documented fields are projected.

Success is signalled by the result flag as well as by the HTTP status. This profile does not read the flag, because a failure document carries result false with error and errorMessage and no items, so a failed collection read fails closed instead of returning an empty list. That residual assumption is recorded rather than hidden.

Rate limits are documented as 120 requests per minute per authenticated user for OAuth requests, with X-RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers. Whether the same number applies to a test token is not documented.
Creating a bookmark needs an explicit link input from the user, and no reviewed destination can carry one, so this profile stays read-only.

rate_limited.documented: Requests are documented as limited to 120 per minute per authenticated user, with X-RateLimit-Remaining reaching 0.

unauthorized.documented: An invalid token answers 401 with an Unauthorized body.

application_failure.documented: A failure document is { result: false, error: ..., errorMessage: ... } with no items, so the collection read fails closed.
